Hi John / Jane —

Thanks again for taking the time earlier today. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery so the security/privacy items are captured: 

Call recap (top-level):
- Use case: Clinical triage assistant; PII elements present in prompts (names, MRNs, partial SSNs).
- Deployment preference: Private deployment (VPC) with US-only data residency.
- Retention expectations: customer wants max 90 days for request logs and explicit deletion on demand for PII.
- Audit & logging: need audit logs, ability to forward to Splunk, and ability to restrict access to raw payloads.
- Egress controls: strict denylist; no external SaaS callbacks allowed except to customer's approved endpoints.

Action items we agreed on:
1) I will send our private/VPC dataflow diagram, high-level security summary, and a draft DPA for initial review (attached).
2) Customer to confirm required retention window (you mentioned 90 days as a target) and any regulated datasets that must never leave a specific subnet.
3) Schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra/security team to walk firewall rules, egress options, and KMS integration.

Preliminary notes from Redwood side:
- Private deployment options: VPC peering (recommended), dedicated transit via IP allowlist, or on-prem/air-gapped appliance for the highest control.
- Logging: we can route request/metrics logs to customer-managed SIEM; access to raw request payloads can be disabled by default and enabled only under agreed processes.
- Encryption: support for customer-managed KMS; HSM options available on dedicated contracts.

Attachments (initial): acmehealth_vpc_requirements.csv, redwood_private_vpc_dataflow.pdf, redwood_security_summary.pdf, dpa_acmehealth_draft.pdf

Proposed times for tech deep-dive: 2026-07-14 09:00-11:00 PT or 2026-07-15 08:00-10:00 PT. Please confirm a 60-90 minute slot and any additional engineers to include.

Thanks —

Thanks for the notes and the attachments. A few clarifying questions before the tech deep-dive: 

1) Persistence of raw inputs: in the private/VPC deployment, will Redwood ever persist raw request payloads outside customer-controlled storage? We need a statement that raw PII will only be persisted to customer-managed volumes or S3 buckets.
2) Logging retention: you mentioned default 30 days — we need confirmation you can set retention to 90 days and provide a way to purge specific records on request.
3) KV/Cache behavior: do any cached KV entries contain PII; how are they encrypted and who has access keys?
4) Egress policy enforcement: can we deny egress to the internet entirely and only allow traffic to our approved endpoints? Is DNS resolution restricted?
5) Key management: can we supply our KMS (AWS KMS) keys and rotate them?
6) On-prem/air-gapped option: we may require an air-gapped deployment for certain regions — what's the timeline and prerequisites for that?

John —

Thanks — great questions. Answers below (high-level) and we will cover more detail on the deep-dive.

1) Persistence of raw inputs:
- Private/VPC: Redwood process nodes can be configured so that request payloads are written only to customer-managed volumes (S3/EBS) mounted in your VPC. By default, we do not retain raw request payloads outside of the configured storage. We will provide an operator-mode setting that disables any transient disk persistence for sensitive fields.

2) Logging retention & purge:
- Retention: configurable per-customer; we support retention policies from 0-365 days. We can set the default to 90 days for Acme and provide an API to purge records by request-id or timestamp range.

3) KV/Cache behavior:
- KV cache can be configured to exclude PII keys. Cached entries are encrypted at rest using customer-managed KMS keys where requested. Access to caches is limited to service accounts; audit trails are available.

4) Egress enforcement & DNS:
- We support strict egress controls: deny-all by default with allowlist for customer endpoints. DNS resolution can be locked down to VPC-provided resolvers only; no external DNS resolution from runtime unless explicitly allowed.

5) Key management:
- Yes — you can supply AWS KMS keys (we integrate via IAM roles) and perform key rotation. We also offer HSM-backed KMS for Dedicated/Private contracts.

6) On-prem/air-gapped option:
- We have an air-gapped on-prem package. Typical delivery timeline is 8-12 weeks depending on certs and network readiness. Pre-reqs: approved network ACLs, physical access windows, and a customer-provided storage target.

Next steps:
- "Technical deep-dive" scheduled for 2026-07-15 08:30 PT — Dev Patel and Neha Kapoor from Redwood will join to walk the network diagram and firewall rules.
- I'll circulate a proposed pre-call agenda in the next email.

Attachments repeated for reference: redwood_private_vpc_dataflow.pdf, redwood_security_summary.pdf, dpa_acmehealth_draft.pdf
